source.text: וַיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֔ן וַיַּ֥ךְ דָּוִ֛יד אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וַיַּכְנִיעֵ֑ם וַיִּקַּ֛ח אֶת־גַּ֥ת וּבְנֹתֶ֖יהָ מִיַּ֥ד פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after thus, and struck David [the] Philistines and subdued them, and took Gath and its daughters from [the] hand of [the] Philistines.

en.L: And it was after this, and David struck the Philistines and subdued them, and he took Gath and its daughters from [the] hand of the Philistines.
en.B: Some time after this, David defeated the Philistines and brought them under his control. He took Gath and its villages out of the Philistines' hands.
en.R: Later David defeated the Philistines and made them give in to him. He took Gath and the villages around it away from the Philistines.

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 18:1-17 retells 2 Samuel 8:1-18
decisions.reason: This chapter gives David's wars and his officials in nearly the same words as 2 Samuel 8, and each record notes where the words differ. As there, "after this" loosely joins the summary of David's wars to the LORD's promise in chapter 17, without dating every battle after it.

decisions.choice: Gath and its villages, where 2 Samuel 8:1 has Metheg-ammah
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:1 says David took "Metheg-ammah", a name whose meaning is not clear. Here David takes Gath, one of the five chief Philistine cities (1 Samuel 6:17), with the villages around it. The Chronicler names the place plainly. 2 Samuel 8:1 also repeats "David" as the subject of "took"; here the verb has no named subject.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the villages that depend on the town; from the hand: from their control
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the smaller settlements around it (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45). "Hand" stands for power, as in 2 Samuel 8:1.

decisions.choice: brought them under his control (Balanced); made them give in to him (Readable); villages
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:1. Literal keeps "daughters"; Balanced and Readable say "villages", as Numbers 21:25 does.

source.text: וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת־מוֹאָ֑ב וַיִּהְי֤וּ מוֹאָב֙ עֲבָדִ֣ים לְדָוִ֔יד נֹשְׂאֵ֖י מִנְחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he struck Moab, and became Moab servants to David bearing tribute.

en.L: And he struck Moab, and Moab became servants to David, bearing tribute.
en.B: He also defeated Moab, and the Moabites became subject to David and brought him tribute.
en.R: David also defeated the Moabites. So they came under David's rule and paid him tribute.

decisions.choice: no measuring of the captives with a line
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:2 tells how David made the Moabite captives lie on the ground and measured them off with a cord, two lengths to be killed and one to live. Here only the victory and Moab's tribute are told.

decisions.choice: servants bearing tribute: a subject people paying regular tribute
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:2. "Servants" here means a nation under David's rule, and the tribute is the gift a subject king brings his overlord (Judges 3:15-18).

decisions.choice: became subject to David (Balanced); came under David's rule (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:2: for a whole nation "servants" means subjects; Literal keeps the word "servants".

source.text: וַיַּ֥ךְ דָּוִ֛יד אֶת־הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־צוֹבָ֖ה חֲמָ֑תָה בְּלֶכְתּ֕וֹ לְהַצִּ֥יב יָד֖וֹ בִּֽנְהַר־פְּרָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And struck David Hadadezer king of Zobah toward Hamath, in his going to set up his hand at [the] river Euphrates.

en.L: And David struck Hadadezer king of Zobah toward Hamath, as he went to set up his hand at the river Euphrates.
en.B: David also defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah, toward Hamath, when Hadadezer went to set up his monument at the Euphrates River.
en.R: David also defeated Hadadezer, the king of Zobah, in the land toward Hamath. This happened when Hadadezer was going to set up a monument to his power by the Euphrates River.

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Samuel 8:3
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:3 calls the king "Hadadezer son of Rehob" and says he went "to restore his hand". Here his father is not named, "toward Hamath" is added, and the verb is "to set up". The name is spelled Hadadezer in both books in the Hebrew text followed here; some older printed Hebrew editions, followed by the King James Version, spell it Hadarezer in Chronicles, with one similar letter changed.

decisions.choice: set up his hand: set up his monument, a sign of his rule
decisions.reason: The verb is used for setting up a standing stone or pillar, and Saul "set up a hand" for himself at Carmel, a victory monument (1 Samuel 15:12; compare 2 Samuel 18:18). So the sense here is most likely a monument claiming the land along the Euphrates. It could also mean, as in 2 Samuel 8:3, to set up his power there; either way he was asserting his rule along the river.

decisions.choice: toward Hamath: the part of Zobah that reached toward Hamath, where the battle was fought
decisions.reason: The ending on "Hamath" marks direction. It places the battle in the north of Zobah, toward the kingdom of Hamath (verse 9). It could also mean that David drove Hadadezer's army back as far as Hamath.

decisions.choice: he: Hadadezer, on his way to the Euphrates
alternatives: David, going to set up his own monument at the Euphrates
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:3: "he" is most likely Hadadezer, setting out to secure his power at the river. It could also mean David, going to set up his own power there (Genesis 15:18).

decisions.choice: when Hadadezer went; a monument to his power (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Hadadezer for "he", following m4. Readable says what the monument stood for.

source.text: וַיִּלְכֹּד֩ דָּוִ֨יד מִמֶּ֜נּוּ אֶ֣לֶף רֶ֗כֶב וְשִׁבְעַ֤ת אֲלָפִים֙ פָּֽרָשִׁ֔ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֣ישׁ רַגְלִ֑י וַיְעַקֵּ֤ר דָּוִיד֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָרֶ֔כֶב וַיּוֹתֵ֥ר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ מֵ֥אָה רָֽכֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And captured David from him [a] thousand chariot[s] and seven thousand horsemen and twenty thousand man [on] foot; and hamstrung David all the chariotry, and left from it a hundred chariot[s].

en.L: And David captured from him 1,000 chariot[s] and 7,000 horsemen and 20,000 men on foot. And David hamstrung all the chariot [horses], and he left of them a hundred chariot[s].
en.B: David captured 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen and 20,000 foot soldiers from him. He hamstrung all the chariot horses but kept enough of them for a hundred chariots.
en.R: David captured 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen and 20,000 foot soldiers. He crippled all the chariot horses so that they could not be used in battle, except for enough to pull a hundred chariots.

decisions.choice: 1,000 chariots and 7,000 horsemen, where 2 Samuel 8:4 has 1,700 horsemen
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:4 has "1,700 horsemen" and no chariots. The Greek translation of Samuel agrees with Chronicles, and the Hebrew of Samuel may have lost the word "chariots" in copying (see the note there). On the size of "thousand" in such counts, see the note at Numbers 1.

decisions.choice: hamstrung the chariot horses: cut the tendons of their hind legs so they could not run
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:4. Joshua did the same at the LORD's command (Joshua 11:6, 9), and Israel's kings were not to gather many horses (Deuteronomy 17:16).

decisions.choice: chariot [horses]; enough of them for a hundred chariots
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:4: Literal brackets "horses"; Balanced and Readable say it plainly, and Readable adds what hamstringing did.

source.text: וַיָּבֹא֙ אֲרַ֣ם דַּרְמֶ֔שֶׂק לַעְז֕וֹר לַהֲדַדְעֶ֖זֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ צוֹבָ֑ה וַיַּ֤ךְ דָּוִיד֙ בַּאֲרָ֔ם עֶשְׂרִֽים־וּשְׁנַ֥יִם אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Aram [of] Damascus to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, and struck David among Aram twenty and two thousand man.

en.L: And Aram of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, and David struck down among Aram 22,000 men.
en.B: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down 22,000 of the Arameans.
en.R: The Arameans from Damascus came to help Hadadezer, the king of Zobah. But David killed 22,000 of them.

decisions.choice: the same as 2 Samuel 8:5, with a later spelling of Damascus
decisions.reason: The verse matches 2 Samuel 8:5. Only the spelling of Damascus differs: Chronicles uses a later form of the name with an extra letter, found in the later books. Aram of Damascus was the Aramean kingdom around that city, in what is now Syria.

decisions.choice: struck down: killed in battle
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:5: with a count of men the verb means that many fell.

decisions.choice: the Arameans
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:5: Balanced and Readable name the people rather than the land.

source.text: וַיָּ֤שֶׂם דָּוִיד֙ בַּאֲרַ֣ם דַּרְמֶ֔שֶׂק וַיְהִ֤י אֲרָם֙ לְדָוִ֔יד עֲבָדִ֖ים נֹשְׂאֵ֣י מִנְחָ֑ה וַיּ֤וֹשַׁע יְהוָה֙ לְדָוִ֔יד בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And put David in Aram [of] Damascus, and became Aram to David servants bearing tribute; and saved Yahweh to David in all that he went.

en.L: And David put [garrisons] in Aram of Damascus, and Aram became servants to David, bearing tribute. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved David wherever he went.
en.B: Then David stationed garrisons in Aram of Damascus. The Arameans became David's subjects and paid him tribute. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave David victory wherever he went.
en.R: Then David put groups of soldiers in the Aramean lands around Damascus. The Arameans came under David's rule and paid him tribute. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made David win wherever he went.

decisions.choice: David put [garrisons] in Aram: the word "garrisons" is understood
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:6 reads "David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus". Here the Hebrew has only "David put in Aram". The word may have dropped out in copying, or the writer left it to be understood from the parallel and from verse 13; the Greek translation of Chronicles has it. Either way the sense is the same as in Samuel.

decisions.choice: servants bearing tribute: as in verse 2
decisions.reason: As with Moab in verse 2, Aram becomes a subject people paying tribute.

decisions.choice: the LORD saved David: the victories are the LORD's doing
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:6, the writer credits the LORD with all of David's success, as he had promised (17:8, "I have cut off all your enemies"). The same sentence closes verse 13.

decisions.choice: [garrisons] (Literal); garrisons (Balanced); groups of soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: Following m1, Literal brackets the word the Hebrew leaves out; Balanced and Readable supply it, as 2 Samuel 8:6 has it.

decisions.choice: gave David victory (Balanced); made David win (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:6: Literal keeps "saved"; in a battle the sense is victory.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח דָּוִ֗יד אֵ֚ת שִׁלְטֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָי֔וּ עַ֖ל עַבְדֵ֣י הֲדַדְעָ֑זֶר וַיְבִיאֵ֖ם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And took David the shields of the gold which were on [the] servants of Hadadezer, and brought them [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them [to] Jerusalem.
en.B: David took the gold shields that Hadadezer's officials had carried, and brought them to Jerusalem.
en.R: Hadadezer's officers had carried shields made of gold. David took them and brought them to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the same as 2 Samuel 8:7
decisions.reason: The verse matches 2 Samuel 8:7 word for word.

decisions.choice: shields: probably shields, perhaps quivers or other gear for display
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:7, the word is rare and its exact sense uncertain; it names objects hung on walls or carried by guards (Song of Songs 4:4; 2 Kings 11:10). Gold ones would have been for display rather than battle.

decisions.choice: officials (Balanced); officers (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:7: a king's "servants" are his officials; Readable says "officers" because they carried shields.

source.text: וּמִטִּבְחַ֤ת וּמִכּוּן֙ עָרֵ֣י הֲדַדְעֶ֔זֶר לָקַ֥ח דָּוִ֛יד נְחֹ֖שֶׁת רַבָּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד בָּ֣הּ׀עָשָׂ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אֶת־יָ֤ם הַנְּחֹ֨שֶׁת֙ וְאֶת־הָֽעַמּוּדִ֔ים וְאֵ֖ת כְּלֵ֥י הַנְּחֹֽשֶׁת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And from Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadadezer, took David bronze much very; with it made Solomon the sea of the bronze and the pillars and the articles of the bronze.

en.L: And from Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took very much bronze. With it Solomon made the bronze Sea and the pillars and the articles of bronze.
en.B: From Tibhath and Cun, towns of Hadadezer, David took a great quantity of bronze. With it Solomon made the bronze Sea, the pillars and the bronze articles.
en.R: David also took a large amount of bronze from Tibhath and Cun, two of Hadadezer's towns. Later Solomon used this bronze to make the huge bronze basin called the Sea, the pillars and the bronze objects for the temple.

decisions.choice: Tibhath and Cun, where 2 Samuel 8:8 has Betah and Berothai
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:8 names the towns Betah and Berothai and calls the taker "King David". Betah and Tibhath may be one name written differently; Cun is otherwise unknown, and may be another name for Berothai or a different town of the same region.

decisions.choice: with it Solomon made the bronze Sea, the pillars and the bronze articles
decisions.reason: This sentence is not in 2 Samuel 8:8. It looks ahead to the temple: the bronze taken in David's wars became the great basin called the Sea, the two pillars and the bronze vessels (1 Kings 7:15-47; 2 Chronicles 4:2-18). Chronicles stresses that David prepared materials for the house his son would build (22:3, 14).

decisions.choice: the bronze Sea: a huge basin in the temple court
decisions.reason: The Sea was a great round bronze basin standing on twelve bronze oxen, in which the priests washed (2 Chronicles 4:2-6).

decisions.choice: Later; the huge bronze basin called the Sea; for the temple
decisions.reason: Readable says that Solomon's work came later and explains what the Sea was and where the bronze was used.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֕ע תֹּ֖עוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ חֲמָ֑ת כִּ֚י הִכָּ֣ה דָוִ֔יד אֶת־כָּל־חֵ֖יל הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־צוֹבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Tou king of Hamath that struck David all [the] army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,

en.L: And Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,
en.B: When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,
en.R: Tou, the king of Hamath, heard that David had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah.

decisions.choice: Tou, where 2 Samuel 8:9 has Toi; "king of Zobah" added
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:9 spells the king's name Toi; the two spellings differ by one letter and name the same man. Here Hadadezer is also called "king of Zobah", as in verses 3 and 5.

decisions.choice: Tou king of Hamath: ruler of a kingdom north of Zobah
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:9. Hamath lay on the Orontes River and later marked the northern edge of Israel's land (Numbers 34:8; 1 Kings 8:65).

decisions.choice: one sentence running into verse 10
decisions.reason: Verse 9 says what Tou heard and verse 10 what he did about it.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח אֶת־הֲדֽוֹרָם־בְּנ֣וֹ אֶל־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ־דָּ֠וִיד לִשְׁאָל־ל֨וֹ לְשָׁל֜וֹם וּֽלְבָרֲכ֗וֹ עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִלְחַ֤ם בַּהֲדַדְעֶ֨זֶר֙ וַיַּכֵּ֔הוּ כִּי־אִ֛ישׁ מִלְחֲמ֥וֹת תֹּ֖עוּ הָיָ֣ה הֲדַדְעָ֑זֶר וְכֹ֗ל כְּלֵ֛י זָהָ֥ב וָכֶ֖סֶף וּנְחֹֽשֶׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: and sent Hadoram his son to the king David to ask to him for peace and to bless him because that he fought against Hadadezer and struck him, for [a] man of wars [of] Tou was Hadadezer; and all articles of gold and silver and bronze.

en.L: and he sent Hadoram his son to King David to ask him about [his] peace and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him, for Hadadezer had been a man of wars [with] Tou; and all [kinds of] articles of gold and silver and bronze.
en.B: he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and congratulate him on fighting against Hadadezer and defeating him, for Hadadezer and Tou had often been at war. Hadoram brought all kinds of articles of gold, silver and bronze.
en.R: So he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and to congratulate him for fighting Hadadezer and defeating him. Hadadezer had been at war with Tou many times. Hadoram brought all kinds of gifts made of gold, silver and bronze.

decisions.choice: Hadoram, where 2 Samuel 8:10 has Joram; the gifts listed without a verb
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:10 calls the son Joram, a name containing a short form of the LORD's name; Hadoram contains the name of the Aramean god Hadad (see the note there). 2 Samuel also says the articles were "in his hand" and lists silver first; here the verse ends simply "and all articles of gold and silver and bronze".

decisions.choice: ask him about his peace and bless him: greet and congratulate him
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:10: asking after someone's peace is the usual greeting, and blessing someone can mean congratulating him on success.

decisions.choice: a man of wars of Tou: one who was often at war with Tou
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:10, Hadadezer was Tou's regular enemy, so David's victory freed Tou from a dangerous neighbor.

decisions.choice: all [kinds of] articles (Literal); Hadoram brought (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The closing words have no verb; they describe what the prince brought as gifts. Balanced and Readable say so, as in 2 Samuel 8:10, and Readable calls the articles gifts.

source.text: גַּם־אֹתָ֗ם הִקְדִּ֞ישׁ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ לַיהוָ֔ה עִם־הַכֶּ֨סֶף֙ וְהַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָשָׂ֖א מִכָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם מֵֽאֱד֤וֹם וּמִמּוֹאָב֙ וּמִבְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וּמִפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וּמֵֽעֲמָלֵֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: Also them dedicated the king David to Yahweh with the silver and the gold which he carried off from all the nations: from Edom and from Moab and from [the] sons of Ammon and from [the] Philistines and from Amalek.

en.L: These also King David dedicated to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with the silver and the gold that he had carried off from all the nations: from Edom and from Moab and from the sons of Ammon and from the Philistines and from Amalek.
en.B: King David dedicated these also to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as he had done with the silver and gold he had carried off from all the nations: from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines and Amalek.
en.R: King David gave these gifts to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} too, along with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations. These nations were Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia and Amalek.

decisions.choice: dedicated: set apart as holy, given over for the LORD's use
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:11. The metal became the LORD's property, kept for his house (verse 8; 1 Kings 7:51). David gives the spoils to the LORD, who gave him the victories (verses 6 and 13).

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Samuel 8:11-12
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:11-12 says the silver and gold "he dedicated" from the nations, where Chronicles says "he carried off"; it lists Aram where Chronicles has Edom (see the note at 2 Samuel 8:12, where the two names differ by one easily confused letter); and it adds "the plunder of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah". Here the two verses are one.

decisions.choice: the Ammonites, the Philistines (Balanced); Ammon, Philistia (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the sons of Ammon", the Hebrew way of naming that people, as in 2 Samuel 8:12. Readable names the lands, as it does there, and makes the list its own sentence.

source.text: וְאַבְשַׁ֣י בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֗ה הִכָּ֤ה אֶת־אֱדוֹם֙ בְּגֵ֣יא הַמֶּ֔לַח שְׁמוֹנָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אָֽלֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And Abishai son of Zeruiah struck Edom in [the] Valley of the Salt, eighteen thousand.

en.L: And Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down Edom in the Valley of Salt, 18,000 [men].
en.B: Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
en.R: Abishai son of Zeruiah killed 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

decisions.choice: Abishai son of Zeruiah struck Edom, where 2 Samuel 8:13 has David making a name by striking Aram
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:13 says "David made a name when he returned from striking Aram in the Valley of Salt, 18,000". Chronicles names the commander who won the battle, Abishai, and the enemy as Edom, which fits the Valley of Salt and the next verse (see the note at 2 Samuel 8:13 on Aram and Edom). The title of Psalm 60 (60:2) credits Joab with 12,000 of Edom in the same valley. The king is credited with what his commanders won, and the different counts may reflect different parts of the campaign.

decisions.choice: Abishai, Joab's brother; the Valley of Salt, near Edom
decisions.reason: Abishai was a son of David's sister Zeruiah and a brother of Joab (2:16; 1 Samuel 26:6). The Valley of Salt lay south of the Dead Sea, toward Edom (2 Kings 14:7).

decisions.choice: 18,000 [men] (Literal); 18,000 Edomites (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:13: Literal brackets the word the number needs; Balanced and Readable join the number to the people.

source.text: וַיָּ֤שֶׂם בֶּֽאֱדוֹם֙ נְצִיבִ֔ים וַיִּהְי֥וּ כָל־אֱד֖וֹם עֲבָדִ֣ים לְדָוִ֑יד וַיּ֤וֹשַׁע יְהוָה֙ אֶת־דָּוִ֔יד בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he put in Edom garrisons, and became all Edom servants to David; and saved Yahweh David in all that he went.

en.L: And he put garrisons in Edom, and all Edom became servants to David. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved David wherever he went.
en.B: He stationed garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became subject to David. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave David victory wherever he went.
en.R: David put groups of soldiers in Edom, and all the Edomites came under his rule. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made David win wherever he went.

decisions.choice: garrisons named once, where 2 Samuel 8:14 says it twice
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:14 reads "he put garrisons in Edom; in all Edom he put garrisons". Here it is said once. Edom, Esau's descendants, now serves the line of Jacob, as Genesis 25:23 and 27:29, 40 had said.

decisions.choice: he: David, whose rule the garrisons served
decisions.reason: After verse 12 "he" could refer to Abishai, who won the battle, but the Edomites become David's subjects, and the parallel in 2 Samuel 8:14 means David. Abishai may have done it in his name.

decisions.choice: as in verse 6
decisions.reason: The refrain of verse 6 is repeated: every victory is the LORD's gift.

decisions.choice: subject to David; gave David victory (Balanced); David put; made David win (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 6. Readable names David for "he", following m2.

source.text: וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ דָּוִ֖יד עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֗י עֹשֶׂ֛ה מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה לְכָל־עַמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And reigned David over all Israel, and was doing justice and righteousness for all his people.

en.L: And David reigned over all Israel, and he was doing justice and righteousness for all his people.
en.B: So David reigned over all Israel, and he did what was just and right for all his people.
en.R: David ruled over all Israel. He was fair to all his people and did what was right for them.

decisions.choice: the same as 2 Samuel 8:15, without the second "David"
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:15 repeats David's name as the subject of "was doing"; otherwise the verse is the same.

decisions.choice: doing justice and righteousness: ruling fairly and rightly
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:15. The pair describes the ideal king (Jeremiah 22:15; Psalm 72:1-2): fair judgments and right dealing that protects the weak.

decisions.choice: was doing: an ongoing practice
decisions.reason: The verb "was" with a participle describes the steady pattern of David's rule. The verse sums up the wars and turns to how David governed; verses 15-17 name the men who served him.

decisions.choice: what was just and right (Balanced); fair ... what was right (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:15: Literal keeps the two nouns; Balanced and Readable use adjectives.

source.text: וְיוֹאָ֥ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֖ה עַל־הַצָּבָ֑א וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן־אֲחִיל֖וּד מַזְכִּֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And Joab son of Zeruiah [was] over the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud [was] recorder,

en.L: And Joab son of Zeruiah [was] over the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud [was] recorder,
en.B: Joab son of Zeruiah was commander of the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
en.R: Joab son of Zeruiah was the army commander. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the royal records.

decisions.choice: the same as 2 Samuel 8:16
decisions.reason: The list of David's officials (verses 15-17) matches 2 Samuel 8:16-18, with the differences noted in verses 16 and 17. Joab, Zeruiah's son, had won his command at the taking of Jerusalem (11:6).

decisions.choice: recorder: the official who kept the royal records
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:16, the title comes from the verb "remember"; he kept the state's records and reminded the king of business (1 Kings 4:3; 2 Kings 18:18).

decisions.choice: one list of officials across verses 15-17
decisions.reason: The list is a series of short clauses joined by "and", running on to the end of verse 17.

decisions.choice: commander of the army (Balanced); army commander (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:16: "over the army" means in command of it.

source.text: וְצָד֧וֹק בֶּן־אֲחִיט֛וּב וַאֲבִימֶ֥לֶךְ בֶּן־אֶבְיָתָ֖ר כֹּהֲנִ֑ים וְשַׁוְשָׁ֖א סוֹפֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: and Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar [were] priests, and Shavsha [was] secretary,

en.L: and Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar [were] priests, and Shavsha [was] secretary,
en.B: Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was secretary;
en.R: Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests. Shavsha was the royal secretary.

decisions.choice: Abimelech son of Abiathar, where 2 Samuel 8:17 has Ahimelech son of Abiathar
decisions.reason: The two names differ by one similar letter in Hebrew, and the Greek translation of Chronicles reads Ahimelech here. Elsewhere Abiathar is the son of Ahimelech (1 Samuel 22:20), and 24:6 has "Ahimelech son of Abiathar"; see the note at 2 Samuel 8:17 on whether the names were reversed in copying or Abiathar had a son named after his grandfather. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Shavsha, where 2 Samuel 8:17 has Seraiah
decisions.reason: The royal secretary is Seraiah in 2 Samuel 8:17, Sheva in 2 Samuel 20:25 and Shisha in 1 Kings 4:3. These are probably spellings of one name, perhaps a foreign one, written differently in each list.

decisions.choice: Zadok son of Ahitub: a priest of Aaron's line
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:17. Chronicles traces him through Eleazar son of Aaron (5:34), and his family served as chief priests from Solomon's reign on.

decisions.choice: the royal secretary
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:17: Readable adds "royal" to show this was a high office at court.

source.text: וּבְנָיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן־יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע עַל־הַכְּרֵתִ֖י וְהַפְּלֵתִ֑י וּבְנֵי־דָוִ֥יד הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים לְיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and Benaiah son of Jehoiada [was] over the Cherethite and the Pelethite; and [the] sons of David [were] the first at [the] hand of the king.

en.L: and Benaiah son of Jehoiada [was] over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David [were] the first ones at the side of the king.
en.B: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were the chief officials at the king's side.
en.R: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the Cherethites and the Pelethites, who were the king's bodyguard. And David's sons were the king's chief officials, serving at his side.

decisions.choice: David's sons were the chief officials at the king's side, where 2 Samuel 8:18 says they were priests
alternatives: the sons of David were priests (2 Samuel 8:18)
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:18 says "the sons of David were priests", using the ordinary word for priest. Chronicles says instead that they were "the first at the king's hand", his highest officials. In Chronicles only the sons of Aaron serve as priests (6:34; 23:13; 2 Chronicles 26:18), so the writer describes the princes' place at court without calling them priests. This may also show how the word in Samuel was understood: as chief ministers of the king rather than men who served at the altar (see the note at 2 Samuel 8:18).

decisions.choice: the first at the king's hand: the highest officials, next to the king
decisions.reason: "First" means foremost in rank, and "at the hand of" means at his side, close to him. The princes held the places of greatest honor and trust at court.

decisions.choice: Cherethites and Pelethites: foreign soldiers who formed the king's guard
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:18: soldiers from the Philistine coast who served as David's personal guard (2 Samuel 15:18; 1 Kings 1:38). Here the Hebrew says Benaiah was "over" them, which 2 Samuel 8:18 leaves unsaid.

decisions.choice: the chief officials at the king's side (Balanced); the king's chief officials, serving at his side (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the first ones"; Balanced and Readable say what being first at the king's side meant. Readable also says who the Cherethites and Pelethites were, as in 2 Samuel 8:18.
